title: Operator rate-limit during control-plane contention causes tenant upgrade stalls — emergency recovery and automated throttling safeguard
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Several private/VPC customer clusters experienced stalled tenant upgrades during a scheduled operator-driven rolling upgrade. Symptom: Helm upgrade hung in 'progressing' for >30 minutes, new nodeagent images not applied, and customer inference tenants reported intermittent 500/503s during the window. This ticket captures the investigation, the emergency mitigations applied, and the post-incident automation to prevent recurrence.
incident_timeline:
2026-03-09 21:10 UTC - Scheduled rolling upgrade campaign started for private operator.
2026-03-09 21:24 UTC - First customer escalation: tenant upgrade stuck in 'waiting' state, GH incident channel created.
2026-03-09 21:30 UTC - Observed spikes of kube-apiserver 429s in affected clusters; control-plane throttling coincident with bursty kubelet reconnects (autoscaler churn).
2026-03-09 21:40 UTC - Operator reconcile loops entered extended exponential backoff; helm release controller held locks waiting for helm timeout retries.
2026-03-09 21:55 UTC - Applied emergency mitigation: pause-the-upgrade for remaining tenants and force-release stuck helm locks using scripted helm-release-unblock tool.
2026-03-09 22:15 UTC - Normal operations restored for most customers; outage window closed.
2026-03-10 - Begin root-cause analysis and hotfix implementation.
root_cause_summary: Primary driver: transient control-plane rate limiting (kube-apiserver 429) caused many operator reconcile loops to back off simultaneously. The operator lacked adaptive concurrency and had a global helm-controller lock pattern that serialized release retries per operator instance. When backoff windows overlapped across tenants, helm timeouts and retries accumulated, effectively stalling upgrades. Secondary factors: aggressive autoscaler-induced kubelet reconnect churn and lack of backpressure shaping on upgrade orchestration.
mitigation_deployed: 1) Immediate: paused in-flight rolling upgrades and executed a safe force-unlock flow to release helm controller locks (internal script: tools/helm_release_unblock.sh). 2) Short-term: limited concurrent reconcile workers and added jitter to reconcile backoffs; rolled operator build private-operator-0.27.3 to affected customers. 3) Monitoring: added a control-plane 429 alert and a per-tenant reconcile latency dashboard.
rollback_steps: If the hotfix causes regressions, rollback plan: 1) Pause upgrade orchestration (console -> private -> upgrades -> pause) 2) Redeploy previous operator image private-operator-0.27.2 via rolling restart with maxUnavailable=1 3) Run helm_release_unblock.sh to ensure no stale locks remain 4) Validate with canary tenant before resuming global upgrades.
verification_steps: Confirm reconciles succeed under induced kube-apiserver 429s using chaos job (runbook/chaos/reconcile-429-test.md)
Smoke: verify nodeagent image updated and traffic routed correctly for two canary tenants (canary-tenant-A, canary-tenant-B)
Metrics: reconcile_latency < 2x baseline and helm_release_lock_count returns to zero within 60s after upgrades are resumed
Logs: no repeated exponential backoff spikes for same reconcile loop beyond configured threshold
follow_up_actions: Automate staggered upgrade window by tenant-weight and region to avoid control-plane bursts
Introduce client-side rate shaping in upgrade orchestrator to limit parallel helm operations per cluster
Add e2e suite that simulates autoscaler churn + operator rolling upgrade to catch regressions in CI
Document incident runbook including safe force-unlock and impact assessment template for support
